paper.title: PhysMem: Scaling Test-Time Memory for Embodied Physical Reasoning
paper.central_claim: A frozen VLM robot planner can learn specific physical principles at test time through a memory loop that generates typed hypotheses from interaction and verifies them before promoting them to guide decisions; "principled abstraction" (verified principles) beats direct experience retrieval (76% vs 23% on medium brick insertion) and yields learning curves in real-world sessions.

evidence.quote: We present PhysMem, a memory framework that enables VLM robot planners to learn physical principles from interaction at test time, without updating model parameters.
evidence.support_explanation: central claim: frozen VLM planner, test-time memory, no weight update

evidence.quote: The system records experiences, generates candidate hypotheses, and verifies them through targeted interaction before promoting validated knowledge to guide future decisions.
evidence.support_explanation: author description of verification step (targeted interaction)

evidence.quote: Hypotheses are judged by action-level outcomes, not episode-level success.
evidence.support_explanation: selection rule for hypotheses is outcome statistics per action type, not designed experiments

evidence.quote: Long-term memory contains verified principles that guide decisions, with importance scores that decay over time
evidence.support_explanation: persistence tier with decay (retention/forgetting)

evidence.quote: The top- k principles and active hypotheses are injected into the VLM prompt
evidence.support_explanation: later use: prompt conditioning of frozen planner

evidence.quote: Our experimental design deliberately separates high-level reasoning from low-level control.
evidence.support_explanation: VLM picks discrete decisions; executor is a fixed motion planner

evidence.quote: MemER [ 55 ] and MemoryVLA [ 51 ] require parameter updates (imitation finetuning or end-to-end VLA training); running their full systems would take us out of the frozen-base setting, so we benchmark training-free proxies that isolate their retrieval mechanism
evidence.support_explanation: neighbour systems are compared only as training-free proxies, not the original systems

evidence.quote: TABLE II: Main results: PhysMem vs. memory paradigms on Brick Insertion (100 episodes per cell, 3 seeds).
evidence.support_explanation: sim comparison denominator: 100 episodes per cell, 3 seeds, same frozen base (Gemini-3-Flash) and budget

evidence.quote: Selective retrieval is no better than no memory: MemER-style retrieval lands at 53% on medium, exactly the No-Memory baseline
evidence.support_explanation: unverified retrieval gives no gain; direct retrieval 23% vs no memory 53% (Table II) is the counter-example motivating verification

evidence.quote: Principle abstraction is the load-bearing component.
evidence.support_explanation: leave-one-out ablation (Table IV) with Gemini-3-Flash, 100 episodes per difficulty

evidence.quote: Verification ensures hypothesis quality before promotion
evidence.support_explanation: w/o Verification lowers medium from 76% to 64% in Table IV (figures in table not in prose quote)

evidence.quote: Without memory (0%), performance remains flat
evidence.support_explanation: real-world learning-curve control: 0% experience vs full memory, 3 runs per condition

evidence.quote: Each task runs for 10–20 episodes.
evidence.support_explanation: real-world denominator is small: 10-20 episodes per task

evidence.quote: Each condition runs 10 trials.
evidence.support_explanation: OOD transfer table: 10 trials per cell

evidence.quote: In contrast, Ball Navigation with new ball types shows that prior knowledge matches zero-shot performance: the new balls have different dynamics, so prior principles do not transfer.
evidence.support_explanation: transfer boundary is stated: prior principles fail under changed dynamics, adaptation needed

evidence.quote: so the planner gets better largely by ruling moves out, not by solving the task end-to-end
evidence.support_explanation: on hard sim tasks gains come from Avoid constraints; limits what is claimed to be learned

evidence.quote: (VLM in real-world, LLM in simulation)
evidence.support_explanation: reflection model differs between real-world (VLM) and simulation (LLM); real-world uses Qwen3-VL async every 15 s

evidence.quote: For VLM planning, we use Gemini-3.0-Flash [ 15 ] with thinking mode.
evidence.support_explanation: real-world planner backbone; single backbone in real world

evidence.quote: The gain from test-time learning then scales with that baseline
evidence.support_explanation: memory gain measured on four VLMs: Gemini-3-Flash +23, GPT-5.1 +14, Qwen3-VL +12, Gemini-ER-1.5 +5 on medium

evidence.quote: and at 3.4\times the token cost the trade-off favors forgetting
evidence.support_explanation: token costs are reported for ablations (relative to PhysMem full)

evidence.quote: Our work focuses on high-level planning rather than low-level control.
evidence.support_explanation: scope limit: high-level planning only; reset needs human intervention

evidence.quote: The issue is that unverified memory hardens into a fixed rule, and a small change in friction or object shape then turns a useful heuristic into a repeated error.
evidence.support_explanation: author gap statement: unverified retrieval memory rigid under physical change

evidence.quote: Hypothesis generation uses Qwen3-VL [ 4 ] , running asynchronously every 15 seconds.
evidence.support_explanation: extra model calls from reflection are not part of the reported token ratios in prose

Algorithm 1 promotes by confidence accumulated from outcomes of past attempts (conf update, >=3 supporting experiences); the material does not describe any procedure that actively designs a discriminating experiment, so "targeted interaction" in the abstract is not a separately specified or ablated mechanism.

signatures.object: Persistent principle store (three-tier memory) conditioning a frozen VLM option-level planner
signatures.information: Planner sees observation, task text and top-k retrieved principles/hypotheses; reflection model (Qwen3-VL real, LLM sim) sees clustered experiences, current principles and hypotheses; executor is a fixed motion planner/policy
signatures.operation: Record experience (o, option, outcome, context, symbolic state) -> resonance check -> cluster by symbolic state -> reflection model drafts typed Avoid/Prefer/Sequence hypotheses -> update confidence by action-level outcomes
signatures.output: Promoted principles (human-readable) injected into the planner prompt; refuted hypotheses removed
signatures.conditions: Tasks recur with hidden physical parameters; outcome signal r in {0,1} available per attempt; symbolic state features available
signatures.feedback: Own attempt outcomes; surprise = low resonance with active principles
signatures.selection_rule: Promote if conf>=tau_p (~0.8) and >=3 supporting experiences; refute if conf<=tau_r with >=2 contradicting; high-resonance experiences only reinforce
signatures.persistence: Episodic buffer (capped N_max), working-memory hypotheses, long-term principles with decay gamma=0.995; supporting episodes folded into the principle on promotion
signatures.later_use: Top-k principles by symbolic filter then semantic ranking are injected at every planning call; low resonance prioritises fresh learning
signatures.claimed_effect: Brick insertion medium 76% vs direct retrieval 23% vs no memory 53%; real-world learning curves; OOD adaptation 10%->40% on new balls
signatures.failure_boundary: Prior principles do not transfer when dynamics change; hard tasks learn mostly Avoid constraints; reset requires humans; no low-level/VLA integration

signatures.information: Same as S1; no designed probing actions are specified in the material
signatures.operation: Withhold hypotheses from the long-term store until outcome-statistics threshold; keep unpromoted hypotheses in working memory and inject them as active hypotheses
signatures.output: Verified principle set vs direct retrieval of raw experiences
signatures.conditions: Enough repeated attempts of the same action type for attribution
signatures.selection_rule: conf threshold plus support count (see S1)
signatures.failure_boundary: Gate quality depends on outcome signal and symbolic-state clustering; "targeted interaction" not separately specified

gap.author_gap: VLM planners know physics in the abstract but cannot predict how a specific object/surface behaves; retrieval-augmented memory applies past experience without verifying it still holds, so it hardens into rigid rules when conditions change.
gap.checked_gap: Partly confirmed inside the paper: direct retrieval (23%) is worse than no memory (53%) on medium and unverified variants drop below the no-memory floor on hard (E009). Whether this holds for the original MemER/MemoryVLA systems is not checked (proxies, E007).

lineage_closest_adjacent.source_versions: Neighbour papers are cited only by reference number; reference list and Section II are not in the fixed material
lineage_closest_adjacent.note: Closest adjacent is Reflexion-style free-form reflection (61% medium vs 76%), which already summarises experience; the delta is typed hypotheses plus a promotion gate plus folding/decay.

gap.residue: Unverified or stale experience degrading decisions when physics changes; context growth over long deployments.
gap.stakes: Repeated errors from rigid heuristics; token growth (3.4x without forgetting).
gap.method_response: Typed hypotheses promoted only after action-level outcome evidence, resonance-based surprise filtering, folding and decay.
gap.remaining_gap: Low-level control and VLA integration; continuous dynamics poorly expressed in text; human resets; real-world scoring and variance not evidenced in available text; verification not shown to involve designed experiments.
unresolved: Related work absent: lineage and novelty versus other test-time memory/skill-library work not checkable here

matches.reason: The operation at deployment is adaptation of a frozen model by injecting retrieved/verified principles as conditioning, with no parameter update; this is the actual operation, not just a mention. Sub-card C03 is not selected because C03 requires a canonical schema plus an upstream phase that teaches the model to parse it and category holdout, none of which PhysMem does; sibling-free parent so sub=null.

executes_pattern.reason: Conditioning without updates is executed; the format-reading and category-holdout parts of the card are not.

resolves_problem.reason: Simulation shows verified abstraction beating retrieval on a controlled benchmark with matched base; real-world evidence has small denominators and unresolved measurement definitions.

condition_checks.reason: Memory variants compared with model and episodes fixed (Table II, Gemini-3-Flash, 100 episodes x 3 seeds).
Tasks recur across episodes; learning curve with 0% vs 100% experience.
Memory is learned on the same stream it is scored on; only the OOD variants are separate.
Novel dynamics tested only for ball types; prior principles fail there.
Leave-one-out ablation with 100 episodes per cell is reported; not_observed does not mean avoided.

matches.operation_match: frozen planner + cross-episode summarisation into typed hypotheses/principles + injection into later contexts; extra: promotion gate, folding, decay.

revision_proposals.text: Single-paper observation: a verification gate between hypothesis and long-term memory (promote on outcome statistics, refute on contradiction, fold supporting episodes) is not part of K302 as written. Needs a second independent paper before a candidate sub-pattern; do not edit cards in-batch.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Retrieved verified principles injected into the prompt of a frozen planner (conditioning, no update) <-> cross-episode notes injected into later planner contexts.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions: Tasks recur; outcome signal per attempt available.
pattern_mapping.differences: K302 is note summarisation; PhysMem adds typed hypotheses, promotion gate, folding/decay. RS card expects trained format parsing and category holdout, which are absent.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On a controlled MuJoCo brick-insertion benchmark with a fixed frozen planner and executor, verified principle memory with promotion/decay beats raw retrieval and unverified memory variants (medium 76% vs 23%/53%), with real-world in-session gains of small denominators.
unresolved: Whether "targeted interaction" is an actual designed-experiment mechanism
assessment.not_claimed: Not our reproduction; all numbers are author-reported. No transfer-level evidence (no new embodiment/sim-to-real).

G.reason: Concrete gap with own measured counter-example: direct retrieval (23%) falls below no memory (53%) on medium brick insertion, motivating verification before application (E022,E009). Nearest neighbours (MemER, MemoryVLA, Reflexion, direct retrieval) are named and run as baselines but two are training-free proxies (E007). Related-work section and references are absent from the fixed material, so lineage and version binding of neighbours cannot be checked; capped at 3.

M.reason: Typed hypotheses, surprise-triggered consolidation, action-level attribution, promotion/refutation thresholds, folding and decay form a coherent mechanism aimed at the stated rigidity problem, and it makes distinguishable predictions (direct retrieval degrades with difficulty 48->23->8 while abstraction holds; leave-one-out drops grow with difficulty). Weakness: the claimed "verification through targeted interaction" is, per Algorithm 1, accumulated outcome statistics rather than designed tests (E024), so the verification mechanism is only partly explained.

X.reason: Operation chain is reconstructable: experience tuple with symbolic state -> resonance check -> clustering and hypothesis generation by a reflection model -> conf update -> promote at tau_p~0.8 with >=3 support, or refute -> fold -> three-tier memory with decay -> top-k injection (E003,E004,E005). Missing from the fixed material: Appendix A constants (tau_r, n_min, alpha, N_max), retrieval details, and how reward r is determined in real-world runs. Transfer and failure boundaries are stated (E015,E016,E021).

E.measurement.reason: Simulation success is binary and environment-checked, but real-world outcomes use plan-quality scores whose exact definition and how outcome r is judged are deferred to Appendices A/F, which are not in the fixed material; the resonance metric depends on a model-judged consistent(e,p). Item cannot be resolved without those sections.

E.causality.reason: Same frozen base, budget and top-K across no-memory, direct retrieval, MemER-style, MemoryVLA-style, Reflexion-style (E008); leave-one-out ablation of resonance, verification, forgetting, working memory (E010,E011); 0/25/50/100% experience and prior x adapt factorial (E012,E014). Remaining gaps: neighbours are proxies (E007), ablations only on one backbone in simulation, token budgets differ across variants, real-world ablation is limited.

E.holdout.reason: Memory is learned and evaluated on the same task stream, so in-stream gains are not held-out generalization; held-out evidence is limited to OOD variants (10 trials/cell, new ball types) and four VLM backbones (E014,E019). No statement on benchmark contamination or on development overlap (tasks were chosen as ones where initial attempts fail).

E.statistics.reason: Sim: 100 episodes per cell, 3 seeds, point estimates only; real world: 10-20 episodes per task, 3 runs per condition, 10 trials per OOD cell; no intervals or paired tests in the available text (E008,E013,E014). Appendix B (full ablations) is absent so provisional.

E.cost.reason: Relative token cost is reported for baselines and every ablation (e.g. no memory 0.40x, PhysMem 1.0x, token memory 2.5x, w/o forgetting 3.4x) with matched task budget and top-K (E008,E020). Omitted: reflection-model calls and wall-clock/latency of real-world runs (E023).
